chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, who said:

A man asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who performs all the circuits of tawaf together and joins them. He said: No; each week is followed by two rakʿahs. Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام only joined them because he was performing tawaf with Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm due to the circumstance of taqiyyah.

So there is no contradiction between these reports and the earlier reports, because the interpretation in them is one of two possibilities: one of them is that the earlier reports are to be understood as referring to merit and recommendation, while the later reports indicate mere permissibility without merit.

The second possibility is that in these reports, joining was only considered disliked in the tawaf of obligation, not in the tawaf of supererogation. That was already clarified in the first two narrations at the beginning of the chapter in his statement: joining between two tawafs is only disliked in an obligatory tawaf, but as for supererogatory tawaf, there is no problem.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary practice due to circumstances requiring concealment
key_terms.الْأَسَابِيعَ: the complete sets of seven circuits in tawaf
key_terms.الْأُسْبُوعُ: one complete set of seven circuits of tawaf
key_terms.رَكْعَتَانِ: the two units of salat (prayer) performed after tawaf
key_terms.فَيَقْرُنُ: he joins one tawaf set to another without separation

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to combine multiple tawaf rounds together before praying their two rakʿahs?
ai.summary: This report discusses the legal ruling on joining multiple tawaf circuits without performing the two rakʿahs after each set. It explains that narrations permitting such joining may be reconciled either by treating them as indicating mere permissibility without merit, or by restricting dislike to obligatory tawaf while allowing it in supererogatory tawaf.
